cards.explanation: The answer is True. Peter says, "…anyone who has suffered in his body is done with sin." (1 Peter 4:1) He ties it to Christ, who suffered in His body, so the resolve he's asking for is the same one. Peter doesn't spell out more than that here, so I won't stuff extra into it either. Plain and powerful, friends.

The answer is the will of God. Peter says this person doesn't live his remaining time on earth "…for human passions, but for the will of God." (1 Peter 4:2) The old way is out and a new reason for living is in. That's a whole new recipe card, friends.

The answer is that they think it's strange. Peter says, "…they consider it strange of you not to plunge with them into the same flood of reckless indiscretion…" (1 Peter 4:4) Picture the whole group heading one direction while you stay put. They look at you like you just walked into a cookie swap and left your tray in the car. Strange, friends, is exactly the word.
The answer is False. The text says they consider it strange, and then "…they heap abuse on you." (1 Peter 4:4) No quiet exit, no peaceful goodbye. I think that's a tough one to walk through, friends.

The answer is the Judge of the living and the dead. Peter says they "…will have to give an account to Him who is ready to judge the living and the dead." (1 Peter 4:5) The abuse is real, but it isn't the final word. God has it, friends.

The answer is pray. Peter says, "Therefore be clear-minded and sober, so that you can pray." (1 Peter 4:7) A clear head helps you talk to God. Mine gets foggy when I smell a fresh batch, but I'm working on it, friends.

The answer is to love one another deeply. Peter says, "Above all, love one another deeply…" (1 Peter 4:8) Above all means he puts it first. The rest of his list, like prayer, hospitality and serving, comes right after it in the same passage. Love sits at the top, friends.

The answer is False. Peter doesn't say love keeps sin from ever happening. He says, "…love covers over a multitude of sins." (1 Peter 4:8) It covers sins over, friends. That's a very different thing from sin never happening.

The answer is without complaining. Peter says, "Show hospitality to one another without complaining." (1 Peter 4:9) Welcome people in and keep the groaning out. Nobody wants a guest list and a grumble, friends.

The answer is serve. Peter says, "…each of you should use whatever gift he has received to serve one another." (1 Peter 4:10) The gift is for the others. It was given so it could go out the door, friends.

The answer is True. Peter says, "If anyone serves, he should serve with the strength God provides…" (1 Peter 4:11) The strength is provided, so you don't have to dig it up on your own. That's a relief, friends.

The answer is so that God may be glorified in all things. Peter says it's "…so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ…" (1 Peter 4:11) That's the reason he gives, and it covers all things. It's not about us getting the spotlight, friends.
